summary:

Standby is a new configuration in the GPT-Live API that lets developers manage periods of inac
text:
GPT-Live-1.1 is now available in the API.

It speaks with more natural and consistent accents across languages, supports lower idle costs with a new standby option, and completes tasks even more reliably.

Standby is a new configuration in the GPT-Live API that lets developers manage periods of inactivity without interrupting the conversation. It's available for both GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1.1.

Set an idle timeout of 5-60 seconds. After that period of silence, the model temporarily pauses, but the WebRTC call stays open at a lower rate ($0.02 per minute vs. the standard $0.05) until someone speaks again.

Sound familiar? GPT-Live-1.1 has powered voice in ChatGPT Plus and Pro since October 15th. Now it can power your apps.

Build better voice agents that can reliably understand precise details like letters and numbers, follow instructions, and delegate complex workflows to the backend model of your choice without breaking the flow of conversation.

summary:

text:
Computer's personalized self-improvement agent, Brain, now automatically creates self-improving agent skills for you.

Brain learns how you work from past sessions and memory, then writes and updates personalized skills for future tasks.

Skills are reusable instructions that guide Computer through recurring tasks. They capture workflow-specific preferences that a general-purpose model can't know in advance.

Brain already maintains a knowledge wiki about each user's work. Skills extend it to procedural memory.

Brain improves skills in a four-stage loop. It finds evidence in past sessions, an improvement agent studies it and proposes a change, checks verify the proposal, and the change is applied.

The improvement agent reads the full record of a session instead of judging from the outcome or a short summary.

It creates a personal skill after observing and identifying recurring patterns, and makes no change when the evidence doesn't support one.

Verification depends on whether a change reaches everyone or one user.

A built-in revision must pass every test scenario, the original must fail at least one, and an engineer must approve it.

Personal skill proposals pass deterministic checks, and an LLM judge audits a sample.

Autonomous skill configuration removes friction and improves results.

In an 8-week randomized test on production traffic, 72.9% of users gained at least one new personal skill with autonomous skill configuration. In the control group, only 6.5% added one manually.

In the same test, the tool call failure rate dropped by 11% across all Computer activity, and by about 7% excluding the system's own background runs.

Medium- and high-dissatisfaction threads per user dropped by 7.6%. Cost and response time didn't measurably change.

Personal skill improvement is now available to all consumer and enterprise subscribers in the US. It's on by default for eligible users and can be turned off in your settings.

Read more: https://www.perplexity.ai/hub/blog/self-improving-skills
